notes.issuer: Islamic Financial Services Board (IFSB), Kuala Lumpur

display_card.one_liner: Fair-dealing rules for how Islamic banks treat customers.
display_card.what_it_is: Guiding principles on ethical conduct of business - honesty, disclosure, fair treatment of clients and Shari'ah compliance in dealings.
display_card.why_it_matters: Customer trust is the product; conduct rules protect it.

notes.applicability: Applies to IIFS conduct toward clients and counterparties.
notes.core_machinery: Sets principles of truthfulness, capability, disclosure, and Shari'ah compliance across the client relationship.

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: Institutions must observe honesty, fair dealing and full disclosure with clients.
Conduct must remain Shari'ah compliant at every stage of the relationship.

notes.issuer: Islamic Financial Services Board (IFSB), Kuala Lumpur
notes.superseded_by: IFSB-31 (2025) - IFSB-31 revises/supersedes the Shari'ah-governance supervision scope

display_card.one_liner: The blueprint for how a bank runs its Shari'ah board and compliance.
display_card.what_it_is: Guiding principles on Shari'ah governance systems - the structure, competence, independence and processes of the Shari'ah board and compliance functions.
display_card.why_it_matters: It is the IFSB parallel to AAOIFI's governance standards - the system that makes compliance real.

notes.applicability: Applies to the Shari'ah governance arrangements of IIFS.
notes.core_machinery: Covers competence, independence, confidentiality and consistency of the Shari'ah board, plus internal Shari'ah review.

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: A competent, independent Shari'ah board must issue and oversee rulings.
An internal Shari'ah review must check ongoing compliance.

display_card.one_liner: Rules so an Islamic bank always has cash on hand.
display_card.what_it_is: Guiding principles on managing liquidity risk - the risk of not having funds when needed - for IIFS (excluding takaful and Islamic funds).
display_card.who_it_applies_to: IIFS excluding takaful institutions and Islamic collective investment schemes.
display_card.why_it_matters: A bank can be profitable yet fail if it runs out of cash.

notes.applicability: Applies to liquidity risk frameworks of IIFS.
notes.core_machinery: Requires governance of liquidity, buffers, and stress-aware funding.

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: IIFS must maintain a sound liquidity risk management framework and adequate buffers.

display_card.one_liner: Testing a bank against imagined bad scenarios.
display_card.what_it_is: Guiding principles on stress testing - checking resilience against severe but plausible shocks - for IIFS.
display_card.who_it_applies_to: IIFS excluding takaful institutions and Islamic funds.
display_card.why_it_matters: Reveals weaknesses before a real crisis does.

notes.core_machinery: Sets premises and scope for regular, board-owned stress testing.

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: IIFS must run regular stress tests covering severe but plausible scenarios.

notes.standard_name: Revised Capital Adequacy Standard for IIFS
notes.issuer: Islamic Financial Services Board (IFSB), Kuala Lumpur

display_card.one_liner: How much capital an Islamic bank must keep as a cushion.
display_card.what_it_is: The revised capital adequacy standard - how to calculate the capital buffer against risks, aligned with global (Basel) standards, adapted for Islamic contracts.
display_card.who_it_applies_to: IIFS excluding takaful institutions and Islamic funds.
display_card.why_it_matters: Capital is the shock absorber that keeps a bank standing.

notes.applicability: Applies to IIFS capital adequacy calculation.
notes.core_machinery: Covers credit, market and operational risk weightings for Islamic contracts and sukuk.

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: IIFS must hold regulatory capital against credit, market and operational risk, using Islamic-contract weightings.

display_card.one_liner: Malaysia's official rulebook for Shari'ah governance in Islamic banks and takaful.
display_card.what_it_is: The BNM policy document setting the Shari'ah governance framework - board, Shari'ah committee, and control functions - for Malaysian Islamic financial institutions.
display_card.who_it_applies_to: Licensed Islamic banks, takaful/retakaful operators, and approved banks with Islamic windows.
display_card.why_it_matters: Malaysia is a lead Islamic-finance market; this is its governance benchmark.

notes.applicability: Applies to Malaysian licensed Islamic financial institutions.
notes.core_machinery: Assigns duties to the board, Shari'ah committee, Shari'ah risk, review, audit and research functions.

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: A Shari'ah committee must oversee compliance; board is ultimately accountable.

display_card.who_it_applies_to: Local banks operating in Saudi Arabia.

notes.core_machinery: Defines Shari'ah committee mandate, independence and the bank's compliance duties.

notes.issuer: Central Bank of the UAE - Higher Shari'ah Authority (HSA)

display_card.one_liner: The UAE's Shari'ah governance rulebook, sitting on top of AAOIFI standards.

display_card.who_it_applies_to: Islamic financial institutions licensed in the UAE.
display_card.why_it_matters: UAE = AAOIFI standards + HSA resolutions layered on top.

notes.applicability: Applies to UAE Islamic financial institutions.
notes.core_machinery: Requires an internal Shari'ah supervision committee, internal Shari'ah control and audit, all under HSA oversight.

key_rules_for_assurance.rule: Each institution must have an internal Shari'ah supervision committee under HSA oversight.
Internal Shari'ah control and audit functions must operate.
